title: Rakuten reports a seven-hour autonomous Claude Code run on vLLM and 79% faster feature delivery
summary: In a 26 June 2025 post on its corporate blog, Rakuten said that machine learning engineer Kenta Naruse asked Anthropic's Claude Code to implement an activation vector extraction method in vLLM, an open-source library with 12.5 million lines of code in multiple programming languages, and that the agent finished the entire job in seven hours of autonomous work in a single run while Naruse wrote no code and only provided occasional guidance; the implementation achieved 99.9% numerical accuracy compared to the reference method. Rakuten also reported that time to market for new features fell by 79%, from 24 days to 5 days, described a test-driven workflow in which Claude Code generates tests and then builds features that pass them, and said AI-powered code review gives feedback on pull requests, but the post does not say whether a human reviewed or merged the vLLM implementation.
verification_note: URL fetched on 2026-10-17; Rakuten Today post dated June 26, 2025, no byline. The vLLM activation-vector task, '12.5 million lines of code', 'seven hours of autonomous work in a single run', 'I just provided occasional guidance', '99.9% numerical accuracy compared to the reference method' and 'Reduced time to market for new features by 79% (from 24 days to 5 days)' are confirmed from the page body. The page names Claude Code but no model version; all metrics are self-reported, and it does not say how the 99.9% figure was measured or whether a human reviewed or merged the vLLM output.
